refuter_findings.location: ## Definition, opening paragraph and sentence stating that symmetry makes the form matrix Hermitian
refuter_findings.evidence: The Definition calls q a “symmetric sesquilinear form” and says “the symmetry of q makes A Hermitian,” but does not state q(u,v)=overline{q(v,u)} or identify an exact earlier definition. For a complex sesquilinear form, that convention is needed to establish Hermitian symmetry and real diagonal values explicitly; the declared matrix-spectral-theorem dependency does not define this form convention.

The Definition asserts “Each returned vector satisfies Ac_j=ρ_jGc_j and c_j^*Gc_k=δ_jk.” The procedure gives B y_j=ρ_j y_j and c_j=G^{-1/2}y_j, but no separate proved result establishes these correctness properties. SCHEMA.md requires algorithmic properties such as correctness to be stated in separate proved lemmas, theorems, propositions, or corollaries.

[F6] says the algorithm “returns the ordered generalized eigenvalues of its exact Gram and form matrices, with a Gram-orthonormal eigenbasis,” and step 1.1 uses this to obtain an eigenbasis of V. The algorithm’s only support is its unproved post-procedure assertion. The omitted calculation is immediate from B y_j=ρ_jy_j and c_j=G^{-1/2}y_j, so this proof gap is nonfatal.
